newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 11.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY

- The Central Committee of China's Communist Party and the State Council, or cabinet, say Party and government departments and officials who spend public funds on extravagant life styles will be severely punished.
- Chinese Premier Li Peng extends thanks to Shoichi Hara, a Japanese rice expert who has been teaching the technique of planting rice with fewer seedlings in China for many years.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Premier Li Peng says only those with advanced technology and reasonable prices can get the upper hand in the highly competitive Chinese market.
- Vice-Premier Wu Bangguo says all random fee collection must be stopped to protect the legal interests of the country's enterprises.
- A memorial service for Bishop Zong Huaide, late chairman of the Chinese Catholic Bishops College, is held in Beijing. He died on June 27.
CHINA SECURITIES
- January-May fixed asset investment hits 356.3 billion yuan, up 14 percent year-on-year.
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS DAILY
- Three Sino-foreign foreign trade joint ventures are set up in Shanghai.
ECONOMIC DAILY
- China's post and telecommunications sector turnover hits 80.91 billion yuan in the first half, up 32.9 percent year-on-year.
- China aims to boost the market share of 12 domestic drinks to 30-40 percent in three to four years.
CHINA BUSINESS DAILY
- The Shanghai Automobile Group announces further price cuts on Santana 2000 sedans.
MARKET DAILY
- China's annual consumption of steel products is expected to reach 119 million tonnes by 2000.
- China's crude oil output and natural gas output are expected to reach 165 million tonnes and 25 billion cubic metres respectively by 2000.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Governor of the Agricultural Bank of China says the bank extended 24.4 billion yuan in loans for poverty-relief projects by end of 1996.
- The State Administration of Foreign Exchange grants foreign exchange business license to the Futian branch of the Shenzhen Development Bank.
- Tianjin-Hong Kong foreign trade volume reaches $290 million in January-May.
- Falling stock prices are squeezing bubbles out of the market.
CHINA DAILY
- The central government is to investigate whether farmland has been used to build golf courses, factories or other developments not stipulated in land-use regulations.
- China refutes accusations that it donated funds to the 1996 U.S. presidential election campaign.
